subject: Discovery Recap & Bake-off Next Steps (Redwood vs vLLM/TGI/Cloud)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Ellis <john.ellis@acme.com>, Sara Nguyen <s.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Redwood bake-off setup

Hi John / Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the candid discussion. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the success criteria you described, and suggested next steps for the competitive bake-off you mentioned (vLLM / TGI / Cloud endpoints). Please correct any inaccuracies.

Summary of pain points
- Unpredictable latency at 95th/99th under burst traffic; spikes impact user-facing freshness.
- High per-token cost on existing cloud-hosted endpoints when serving many smaller requests.
- No consistent A/B tooling to measure quality regressions across model variants.

Current stack
- Frontend + API on AWS, inference currently on managed cloud endpoints (multi-tenant).
- Some internal experiments with vLLM on k8s for on-premish latency gains; TGI used by one team for local testing.
- Persistence: S3 + Redis cache for KV; no dedicated inference cluster today.

Stated goals / success criteria (from call)
- P95 latency < 120ms for 2–4k token context workloads; P99 < 350ms for steady state.
- Comparable/worse-case quality: no more than 3% drop in top-line eval (intent match) vs current model baseline.
- Unit cost target: <= 60% of current per-token spend for steady throughput (with occasional burst capacity).
- Observable rollout and regression alerts integrated with your monitoring.

Suggested bake-off approach
1) Redwood provides a 2-week isolated evaluation environment (dedicated capacity) and a bake-off template for results capture.
2) We'll run parallel endpoints: Redwood Hosted (dedicated pool), configured vLLM on your k8s (if you want us to run it), and current cloud endpoints you provided.
3) Benchmark suite: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, cost per 1M tokens, and a quality eval over your 500-case prompt set.
4) Acceptance criteria: explicit latency + quality thresholds (see attached template).

Requested from Acme
- Representative prompt set (CSV) + sample production traffic profile (token lengths, concurrency).
- The primary model(s) you want in the comparison (model name + size + any quantization/FP settings).
- Any non-functional constraints (VPC-only, encryption at rest, SOC2 requirements).

Next steps / proposed timeline
- If you confirm, we’ll share the Redwood bake-off template and a short runbook (1 business day) for required artifacts.
- Redwood will standby a small dev team (Dev + Rishi) to help configure and run benchmarks next week.
- Joint review call at end of week 2 to go over benchmark outputs and recommended configuration.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-template.xlsx (bake-off checklist + metrics sheet)

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
Note: call recording and logs can be shared after you confirm test dataset access.
From: John Ellis <john.ellis@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Nguyen <s.nguyen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Redwood bake-off setup

Thanks Marissa — this looks right to me and mirrors what we discussed. A few quick clarifications: 

- For latency targets, the 2–4k token context is our upper bound; most production calls are in the 200–800 token range. The 95th in-production spike is what’s hurting the UX.
- For quality eval, we have a labeled set (approx. 500 prompts) with intent + correctness flags. I’ll share that as a CSV shortly.

I've looped procurement (procurement@acme.com) to start any required paperwork. Procurement will want a list of all deliverables (SOC2, SSO / SAML support, data handling), and a cost estimate by configuration (dedicated vs hosted).

We can provide the model names — primary candidate is "acme-embedding-3b" for embeddings and "open-llm-13b" for generation. We’re also interested in seeing how quantized variants behave (int8/4).

Attachments: acme-bakeoff-criteria.docx (acceptance criteria outline)

John
--
John Ellis
Director, ML Platforms
Acme Corp
john.ellis@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Next Steps — Redwood bake-off setup

Thanks John — appreciated. I’ve attached the bake-off template (same as referenced) and a short plan below to keep coordination simple.

Proposed Redwood-run bake-off plan (we can adapt):
- Day 0: Access & onboarding — we exchange test dataset + credentials (short checklist).
- Day 1–3: Baseline runs (your cloud endpoints + vLLM/TGI configuration if you want Redwood to run those for parity).
- Day 4–10: Configuration tuning (batching, quantization profiles), rerun benchmarks.
- Day 11–14: Final runs, cost analysis, and joint review.

Benchmarks we’ll capture (examples):
- Latency: p50 / p95 / p99 across representative QPS and burst windows.
- Throughput: tokens/sec under steady-state worker configuration.
- Cost: effective $/1M tokens at the observed throughput.
- Quality: intent accuracy + response-level BLEU/ROUGE where applicable (we’ll use your labeled 500-case set).

Acceptance checklist (high level) — from template:
- P95 < 120ms for requested context sizes OR explain tradeoffs.
- Intent accuracy delta vs baseline <= 3%.
- Cost improvement >= 40% over current baseline (if not, note config needed).
- No high-severity security blockers (SOC2, SSO) for Dedicated option.

Can you confirm:
1) Which models you want included? (open-llm-13b, acme-embedding-3b, quantized variants)
2) Who is our procurement contact (I see procurement@acme.com CC'd — please share a direct name if possible).
3) Any strict blackout windows for running benchmarks?

We’ll put together a short runbook and a pre-populated benchmarks sheet (attached). Happy to run the vLLM/TGI variants in your environment if you prefer Redwood to manage parity runs — that typically speeds up comparisons.

I’ll have Dev and Rishi stand by for onboarding once you confirm.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa — thanks. We’re aligned on the plan. A couple of additions from procurement:

- Procurement requests: SOC2 Type II report, data processing addendum (DPA), and SAML SSO implementation notes.
- For the bake-off we’ll supply the labeled 500-case CSV and a small live traffic sample (anonymized) by EOD tomorrow.
- Acceptance criteria: we’ll run Redwood, vLLM (our k8s cluster), and the cloud endpoints in parallel. Decision will weigh latency, cost, and quality — but any solution that fails the P95 threshold will be deprioritized.

Attached: acme-bakeoff-criteria.docx (procurement + acceptance checklist)

Procurement point: please send a preliminary cost estimate for both (1) Redwood Dedicated eval (reserved short-term) and (2) Hosted API comparison so procurement can preliminarily size the order.

I’m ok for Redwood to run parity runs for vLLM/TGI if you include the run methodology in the runbook.
